questions.question: Objects `o#42 : Order` and `c#7 : Customer` are connected by the `places` association — in UML, what is that specific object-to-object connection called?
questions.explanation: A link is an instance of an association connecting particular objects, just as an object is an instance of a class.

questions.question: On a class diagram, `Employee` connects back to `Employee` through `manages`, where one instance supervises others — what kind of association is this?
questions.explanation: Both association ends attach to the same class: a reflexive (self) association.

questions.question: A Student–Course many-to-many must store `grade` and `semester` — attributes belonging to each pairing rather than to either class — which UML construct models this?
questions.explanation: Promoting the association to a class lets it carry its own attributes: an association class such as Enrollment.

questions.question: `Bank —1..*→ Account` is refined so `accountNumber` on the Bank end selects a single Account — which UML feature reduced the multiplicity?
questions.explanation: A qualifier partitions the target set so one qualifier value picks one instance, turning 1..* into 1: a qualified association.

questions.question: UML draws `Person —/ancestor— Person` with a slash because ancestry is computed by chaining `parent` links and never stored — what kind of association is this?
questions.explanation: The slash marks a derived association whose links are calculated from other relationships rather than stored.

questions.question: A diagram writes `{ordered}` in braces beside a Playlist–Song association to require a sequence — what is this UML construct called?
questions.explanation: Braces attach a constraint: a rule the relationship must satisfy, in this case ordering.

questions.question: A `Payment` links to `CreditCard` or `Cash`, but never both at once, and the diagram marks the two associations for mutual exclusivity — which constraint is applied?
questions.explanation: An xor constraint makes the associations mutually exclusive — at most one may be instantiated at a time.

questions.question: `Project —1..*→ Task` must keep its tasks in execution sequence — which UML annotation expresses that ordering on the association?
questions.explanation: The {ordered} constraint declares that the associated elements form an ordered sequence.

questions.question: `invoice.getCustomer().getAddress().getCountry().getCode()` drills through a chain of strangers to reach a distant field — which design principle does this train-wreck chain violate?
questions.explanation: Each call should reach only an immediate collaborator; the chain 'talks to strangers', violating the Law of Demeter.

questions.question: On an Employee–Employee `manages` association, one end is labeled `manager` and the other `subordinate` — what are these labels called?
questions.explanation: Labels on association ends naming the part each class plays are role names.

questions.question: A hollow diamond sits on the `Team` end of Team–Player, and a Player may belong to several Teams at once — what is the UML specification's formal name for this relationship?
questions.explanation: A hollow-diamond whole-part link with non-exclusive parts is formally 'shared aggregation' in the UML specification.

questions.question: A filled diamond sits on the `Document` end of Document–Page, where deleting the Document destroys its Pages — what is the UML specification's formal name?
questions.explanation: A filled-diamond exclusive-ownership link with lifecycle control is formally 'composite aggregation'.

questions.question: On a navigable association, a small 'x' is drawn at the `Order` end — what does that mark tell designers about reaching Order objects?
alternatives: Orders cannot be reached from the other side
questions.explanation: An x marks a non-navigable association end: objects there are not reachable from the classifier at the other end.

questions.question: To express 'a Customer may place 0 to many Orders', where exactly on the Customer–Order relationship is `0..*` written?
questions.explanation: Multiplicity is an adornment of the member end — the 0..* goes at the Order end of the association.

questions.question: Rather than `class Stack extends ArrayList`, which leaks insert() and remove(), a design holds `private List items` and exposes only push/pop that forward to it — which GoF principle is applied?
questions.explanation: Reusing List by containment instead of inheritance keeps the interface minimal: 'favor composition over inheritance'.

questions.question: `class Car { private final Engine engine = new Engine(); }` where the Engine cannot outlive the Car — which relationship is this?
questions.explanation: Exclusive ownership with a shared lifetime is composition.

questions.question: In UML, a hollow (unfilled) diamond on the whole end represents which relationship?
questions.explanation: The hollow diamond denotes aggregation; the filled diamond denotes composition.

questions.question: `class Order { Customer customer; }` where the Customer exists independently of any Order — which relationship?
questions.explanation: An independent, non-owning link between objects is a plain association.

questions.question: `void report(Printer p){ p.print(); }` uses Printer only as a parameter with no stored field — which UML relationship?
questions.explanation: A transient use relationship (parameter/local only) is the weakest link: dependency.

questions.question: In UML, `class ArrayList implements List` is drawn as a dashed arrow with a hollow triangle — what is this called?
questions.explanation: A class implementing an interface is a realization relationship.
